text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000282 bills 99215 far above risk-adjusted expectation, mostly on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions, and the few returned charts are too thin to confirm or refute the billed levels.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The billing pattern leans toward upcoding. The excess 99215 use is not explained by panel acuity: most 99215s fall on patients with no or one chronic condition. The sampled low-complexity claims show simple presentations billed at the top level, such as rash (C0136469, C0136499), low back pain (C0136443, C0136672) and urinary infection (C0136697, C0136972). The provider also bills 99214 heavily, including on zero-condition patients (C0136609, C0136872). The main ambiguity is documentation: only 3 documented 99215 claims came back, all supported at high MDM, and the one cloned-note signal (moderate-plus data reviewed with no lab line) is weak. The charts therefore neither confirm nor rule out inflation. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims and check whether they show high-complexity decision-making and the time to support it, or templated or inflated notes."}
